sections.What we use it for:
Zensical comes from the team behind Material for MkDocs, and reads the `mkdocs.yml` that MkDocs and Material read. It renders the theme's `features:` and `palette:` blocks, builds the search index, and writes a redirect page for each entry in `redirect_maps`. The redirect page keeps the anchor. `theme.variant: classic` keeps the look Material gave the site.

`strict: true` turns a dead link or a dead anchor into a failed build. A page the navigation does not list passes the build, so `NavigationTests` in `kac.tests` covers that case.
sections.Status:
Approved for the 0.0 line, and pinned at 0.0.72 in `docs/requirements.txt`. Zensical publishes a release every few days and makes no promise about stability or about how long it reads `mkdocs.yml`. Each Dependabot pull request meets the strict build before it merges.

`mkdocs.yml` still builds the same site under MkDocs 1.6.1 with Material 9.7.7, so leaving Zensical is a change to `docs/requirements.txt` and to the build command in two workflows. The review date falls before Material's critical fixes end on 2027-05-05.
sections.Accessibility:
Assessed against [WCAG 2.2 AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) at 0.0.72 with the `classic` variant, by building the site with the pinned version and reading the HTML it emits. [std-A11Y](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/297de4eed28ec0ed420ceb18c1b890124924676e/examples/dog-fooding/standards/accessibility.md) states the rules the assessment checks against.

The theme supplies what a Markdown author cannot. `<html lang="en">` states the language of every page. A "Skip to content" link is first in the keyboard tab order. The header logo is an image whose alternative text is the site's name, and the navigation and search buttons each carry a visually hidden label. Each page's `<title>` names the page, the home page included. Contrast comes from the `default` and `slate` schemes with `indigo` primary, which are the theme's own and unchanged. `docs/assets/extra.css` sets two margins and nothing else.

Two things fall short. Nobody has run the site through a screen reader or a contrast checker, so the contrast of the two schemes is taken from the theme and not measured here. A Mermaid diagram renders as an SVG that the theme gives no text alternative, so the prose beside it is the only way to read what it says.
sections.Licence and obligations:
The package declares MIT, and its own code is MIT. The wheel also ships five icon sets under `zensical/templates/.icons/`, each with its own licence file: Material Design Icons from the Pictogrammers under Apache-2.0, Font Awesome Free under CC-BY-4.0, GitHub's Octicons under MIT, Simple Icons under CC0-1.0 and Lucide under ISC. An icon put on a page comes under its own set's terms, and CC-BY-4.0 asks for attribution.

The theme's JavaScript reaches every published page. Its licence file names clipboard and escape-html under MIT, rxjs under Apache-2.0, and focus-visible under the W3C Software Notice. Material's bundle shipped the same four packages.

The compiled core bundles 308 Rust components, listed in the CycloneDX file the wheel carries under `sboms/`. Each is under a permissive licence, or offers one as a choice, and none reaches the published site.
